description: When learners study material whose essential elements and organisation they cannot yet pick out for themselves, adding cues that highlight those elements and how they connect (headings, an outline, highlighting, arrows, colour links between words and picture, spoken emphasis) is expected to improve learning over the same material without cues, by a small-to-medium amount in the meta-analyses the wiki records; the claims test this directly and report it weakening or reversing for learners who already know the material, and helping only for what is cued.
title: Signaling Principle

description: For a learner preparing for a risky, costly, rare or invisible performance, repeated runs in a simulation that keeps the task's decisions and cues, guided during exploration and followed by feedback or a debrief, are expected to improve performance on the represented task more than no simulated practice, with more immersion adding nothing by itself; claims test simulation against no intervention, passive and active instruction (no advantage over active methods) and guided against free VR exploration, but not the debrief, dose or fidelity.
title: Simulations & Immersive Virtual Environments
